newsitem.title: UK: Copper prices extend rally, then tumble.
newsitem.headline: Copper prices extend rally, then tumble.

text.p: Copper prices extended a sudden rally above $2,000 a tonne on Monday to their highest level for 2-1/2 months then dropped to end lower on the day.

But neither copper nor any other commodity could match the action in crude oil, up $1 per barrel to around $21.85, after the United Nations delayed an Iraqi oil-for-food exchange in response to Iraq's military incursion into its Kurdish region.
London gold closed at $386.90 after $386.35 on Friday in a very quiet market.
Bullion trading was subdued, as were most other non-oil commodity markets, because of the U.S. Labour Day holiday.
London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices finished the afternoon session at $2,026 per tonne, $13 down on the day and $139 below the new high at $2,165.
The shortlived advance was made in very thin volume that exaggerated the impact on the market.
The early gain was a heady mix of short-covering and options-related buying in reaction to an early advance.
Some key commodity prices at 1600 GMT
